```{r}
#| label: setup-data
#| include: false
#| eval: true
# Single source of truth for every number and chart in this deck.
library(tidyverse)
library(jsonlite)

# ---- M830169: median age by gender/marriage order ----
raw169 <- read_csv("data/raw/M830169_raw.csv", skip = 10, col_names = FALSE)
years_header <- raw169 |> slice(1) |> select(-1) |> unlist() |> as.numeric()

marriage <- raw169 |>
  set_names(c("X1", as.character(years_header))) |>
  slice(-1) |>
  mutate(label = str_trim(X1),
         is_header = str_detect(label, " - "),
         type   = if_else(is_header, str_split_i(label, " - ", 1), NA),
         gender = if_else(is_header, str_split_i(label, " - ", 2), NA)) |>
  fill(type, gender, .direction = "down") |>
  mutate(order = if_else(is_header, "All", label)) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(X1,label,is_header,type,gender,order),
               names_to = "year", values_to = "age") |>
  filter(type == "Total Marriages",
         order %in% c("First Marriages","Remarriages"),
         as.integer(year) >= 2003, as.integer(year) <= 2024) |>
  # tidyr::pivot_wider() uses EVERY remaining column as an implicit id_col --
  # unlike pandas' pivot_table, it does not stop at just the index you have in
  # mind. X1/label/is_header still differ between the "First Marriages" row
  # and the "Remarriages" row for the same year, so without dropping them
  # first, pivot_wider produced 44 rows (one per source row) instead of 22
  # (one per year). Select down to only what's needed before pivoting.
  select(year, gender, order, age) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(gender, order), values_from = age) |>
  rename(groom_first   = `Grooms_First Marriages`,
         groom_remarry = `Grooms_Remarriages`,
         bride_first   = `Brides_First Marriages`,
         bride_remarry = `Brides_Remarriages`) |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  mutate(groom_gap = round(groom_remarry - groom_first, 1),
         bride_gap = round(bride_remarry - bride_first, 1))

stopifnot(nrow(marriage) == 22,
          all(marriage$groom_gap > 0, marriage$bride_gap > 0),
          n_distinct(marriage$year) == nrow(marriage))

# ---- M830170: age-band counts, Total Marriages only ----
raw170 <- read_csv("data/raw/M830170_raw.csv", skip = 10, col_names = FALSE)
years170 <- raw170 |> slice(1) |> select(-1) |> unlist() |> as.numeric()

bands <- raw170 |>
  set_names(c("X1", as.character(years170))) |>
  slice(-1) |>
  mutate(label = str_trim(X1),
         gender = if_else(str_detect(label, " - "), str_split_i(label, " - ", 2), NA),
         age_band = if_else(str_detect(label, " - "), NA, label)) |>
  fill(gender, .direction = "down") |>
  filter(!is.na(age_band)) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(X1, label, gender, age_band), names_to = "year", values_to = "count") |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  # same pivot_wider fix as above -- drop X1/label before pivoting, not after
  select(year, gender, age_band, count) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = age_band, values_from = count) |>
  select(year, gender, `Under 20`, `20-24`, `25-29`, `30-34`, `35-39`,
         `40-44`, `45-49`, `50-54`, `55-59`, `60 & Over`) |>
  arrange(year, gender)

# 21 published years (2003-2023) x 2 genders. NOT 44/22-years -- SingStat's
# age-band table doesn't yet cover 2024 at the time this was pulled.
stopifnot(nrow(bands) == 42)

# ---- JS data arrays for the D3 charts ----
marriage_js <- marriage |>
  transmute(y = year, gf = groom_first, gr = groom_remarry, bf = bride_first, br = bride_remarry)
marriage_data_json <- toJSON(marriage_js, dataframe = "rows", auto_unbox = TRUE)

bands_wide <- bands |>
  mutate(row = pmap(list(`Under 20`,`20-24`,`25-29`,`30-34`,`35-39`,`40-44`,`45-49`,`50-54`,`55-59`,`60 & Over`),
                     function(...) unname(c(...))))
groom_bands_list <- setNames(bands_wide$row[bands_wide$gender == "Grooms"],
                              bands_wide$year[bands_wide$gender == "Grooms"])
bride_bands_list <- setNames(bands_wide$row[bands_wide$gender == "Brides"],
                              bands_wide$year[bands_wide$gender == "Brides"])
groom_bands_json <- toJSON(groom_bands_list, auto_unbox = TRUE)
bride_bands_json <- toJSON(bride_bands_list, auto_unbox = TRUE)

# ---- A1: first-marriage age vs year, per gender ----
fit_g <- lm(groom_first ~ year, data = marriage)
fit_b <- lm(bride_first ~ year, data = marriage)
ci_g  <- confint(fit_g)["year", ]; ci_b <- confint(fit_b)["year", ]
r2_g  <- summary(fit_g)$r.squared;  r2_b  <- summary(fit_b)$r.squared
p_g   <- summary(fit_g)$coefficients["year","Pr(>|t|)"]
p_b   <- summary(fit_b)$coefficients["year","Pr(>|t|)"]
# Welch-style t-test on the difference between the two slopes
se_diff  <- sqrt(summary(fit_g)$coefficients["year","Std. Error"]^2 +
                  summary(fit_b)$coefficients["year","Std. Error"]^2)
t_diff   <- (coef(fit_b)["year"] - coef(fit_g)["year"]) / se_diff
df_diff  <- nrow(marriage) + nrow(marriage) - 4

# ---- A2: gap (remarry - first) vs year, per gender ----
fit_gg <- lm(groom_gap ~ year, data = marriage)
fit_bg <- lm(bride_gap ~ year, data = marriage)
ci_gg  <- confint(fit_gg)["year", ]; ci_bg <- confint(fit_bg)["year", ]
r2_gg  <- summary(fit_gg)$r.squared; r2_bg <- summary(fit_bg)$r.squared
p_gg   <- summary(fit_gg)$coefficients["year","Pr(>|t|)"]
p_bg   <- summary(fit_bg)$coefficients["year","Pr(>|t|)"]

# ---- A3: correlation between groom and bride first-marriage age ----
ct <- cor.test(marriage$groom_first, marriage$bride_first)
gender_gap <- marriage$groom_first - marriage$bride_first
```

# Original Work {.section-divider}

::: section-sub
Assessing the article's headline and its chart
:::

## The article behind our project {.smaller}

On 15 July 2024, Mothership.SG published a news piece on Singapore's latest marriage and divorce figures, drawn from the Department of Statistics' 2023 report [@mothership2024].

```{=html}
<div style="display:flex;gap:36px;align-items:flex-start;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-top:12px;">
  <figure style="flex:0 0 400px;max-width:400px;margin:0;border:1px solid #e4ddd2;border-radius:10px;overflow:hidden;box-shadow:0 3px 12px rgba(35,48,74,.14);background:#fff;">
    <div role="img" aria-label="Mothership.SG article, 15 July 2024" style="width:100%;height:230px;background-image:url('https://static.mothership.sg/1/2024/07/divorce-sg.jpg');background-size:cover;background-position:center;"></div>

      <div style="font-size:10.5px;letter-spacing:.09em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#b5651d;font-weight:700;">Mothership.SG &middot; News &middot; 15 July 2024</div>
      <div style="font-family:'Source Serif 4',Georgia,serif;font-weight:700;font-size:17px;color:#23304a;margin-top:3px;line-height:1.15;">Couples marrying later in S'pore, divorces up 0.2% in 2023</div>
      <div style="font-size:11.5px;color:#5f6b7a;margin-top:4px;">By Seri Mazliana</div>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <div style="flex:1 1 420px;min-width:320px;font-family:Inter,sans-serif;color:#23304a;">
    <div style="font-weight:700;font-size:22px;margin-bottom:10px;">What the article reported</div>
    <ul style="margin:0 0 10px;padding-left:1.15em;line-height:1.45;font-size:18px;">
      <li style="margin-bottom:6px;"><b>Fewer marriages:</b> 28,310 registered in 2023, down 3.7% from 2022's record high of 29,389.</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:6px;"><b>Not a collapse:</b> that total is close to pre-pandemic levels, so the dip is a return to normal.</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:6px;"><b>Marrying later:</b> median age 31 for men and 29.5 for women, up from 30.2 and 28.1 a decade earlier.</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:6px;"><b>Divorces up 0.2%:</b> 7,118 marriages ended in divorce or annulment.</li>
      <li style="margin-bottom:6px;"><b>Backed by one chart:</b> the article uses a single SingStat chart to prove the marrying-later point.</li>
      <li><b>Why we chose it:</b> that one chart is what we set out to critique and rebuild.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>
```

## The question behind the headline {.smaller}

Between 2003 and 2024, the median age at first marriage in Singapore rose from 29.1 to 31.1 for grooms and from 26.6 to 29.6 for brides [@singstat_m830169].
Among those who remarry, the shift is larger still.

::: box
Singaporeans are not rejecting marriage.
They are **delaying** it, and who delays the most is changing.
:::

Three questions drive our project:

- How wide is the gap between first-marriage and re-marriage age, and has it grown?
- Are grooms and brides changing at the same pace, or is one moving faster?
- Can a single interactive chart carry all of that without asking the reader to track four lines at once?

::: small
Data: Singapore Department of Statistics, Table M830169.
Original reporting: Mothership.SG (15 July 2024) [@mothership2024].
:::

## The original visualization {.smaller}

Here is the chart the article used to back its "marrying later" point, taken straight from SingStat [@mothership2024].
It plots four series from 2003 to 2023: grooms and brides, each at first marriage and re-marriage.

::::: columns
::: {.column width="58%"}
![Original static four-line chart, Mothership.SG (2024), sourced from SingStat.](https://static.mothership.sg/1/2024/07/Screenshot-2024-07-15-at-7.46.14%E2%80%AFPM.png){width="100%"}
:::

::: {.column width="42%"}
**The story it tells**

All four lines climb across twenty years.
Re-marriage sits roughly ten to fourteen years above first marriage throughout.

The broad message lands in a glance: people are marrying later, first marriage or not.
:::
:::::

::: small
Grooms and brides, at first marriage and re-marriage.
Median age on the y-axis, year on the x-axis.
:::

## What the original does well {.smaller}

::: box
Four dimensions in one plot: **year** (x-axis), **median age** (y-axis), **gender** (colour), **marriage type** (line style).
No flipping between charts.
:::

- **Solid versus dashed reads intuitively.** A dashed line for re-marriage follows a visual grammar most readers already know, so the two marriage types separate without constant legend checks.
- **Direct data labels remove guesswork.** Values are printed beside plotted points, which matters for a static image with no hover tooltip to fall back on.
- **The warm colour pairing stays coherent.** Red for grooms and orange for brides read as one family with two variants, suiting two genders inside one institution.

A non-specialist takes in the headline, that people marry later, within a few seconds.

# Our Improvements {.section-divider}

::: section-sub
Redesigning the visualization for clarity
:::

## Where it falls short {.smaller}

::: fit-col
| \# | Weakness |
|----|----|
| **W1** | The two closely spaced line pairs are hard to differentiate. The eye keeps returning to the legend |
| **W2** | The gender comparison readers want is buried under two encodings at once |
| **W3** | Only four points unevenly spaced across twenty years, so most of the series is invisible. The static format also cannot answer specific values |
| **W4** | The most interesting number (closing gender gap) is never shown |
| **W5** | Median age is the only statistic shown. There is no sense of spread, so readers cannot tell whether that typical age represents most couples or hides a wide range |
| **W6** | The colour choice may not hold up for all readers. Red and orange sit close for readers with colour vision deficiency |
:::

::: small
One root cause: The chart serves a detailed dataset through a format, four overlapping static lines with only four labelled points, that cannot show gaps, trends, or precise intermediate values without extra work from the reader.
:::

## Our proposed redesign: an interactive dumbbell {.smaller}

Each bar spans one year.
The **gap** from the first-marriage age to the re-marriage age **becomes the visual subject** rather than something the reader calculates.
A gender toggle shows one set of dumbbells at a time.
Every row also carries its own age-band histogram as a background ridge, so the distribution and the dumbbell share one axis instead of living in separate charts.

::: fit-col
| Fixes | Improvement |
|----|----|
| **W1, W2** | Dumbbell layout toggled by gender, so no second pair of lines competes for attention |
| **W3** | Every year from 2003 to 2024 plotted, both endpoints labelled for all 22 years |
| **W4** | The numeric gap printed on every connector |
| **W4, W5** | Label both endpoints of every dumbbell with their exact value |
| **W5** | A background histogram layered behind every row's dumbbell with optional mean/mode markers, so the median line is no longer the only statistic on screen |
| **W5, W6** | An interactive toggle. Only one gender's colour is ever on screen |
:::

::: small
One shared plot, one coordinate system: The histogram and the dumbbell are two geoms layered on the same axes and not two separate charts, so the improved visualization stays a single plot rather than a dashboard.
The background histogram draws on SingStat's age-band counts, published for all marriage orders combined rather than split by first marriage versus re-marriage [@singstat_m830170].
:::

## Improved visualization {background-color="#faf8f4"}

```{r}
#| label: emit-chart-data
#| echo: false
#| eval: true
#| results: asis
# Injects MARRIAGE_DATA / GROOM_BANDS / BRIDE_BANDS as real <script> globals,
# generated from data/clean/*.csv via the setup-data chunk above -- these used
# to be hand-typed JS arrays in _head-include.html. AGE_BANDS, BAND_MID and the
# groom/bride image URLs are unchanged and still live in _head-include.html
# since they're static config, not analysis data.
cat(
  "<script>\n",
  "var MARRIAGE_DATA=", marriage_data_json, ";\n",
  "var GROOM_BANDS=", groom_bands_json, ";\n",
  "var BRIDE_BANDS=", bride_bands_json, ";\n",
  "</script>\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

```{=html}
<div class="dumbbell-wrap" style="max-width:1040px;margin:0 auto;">
  <div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-start;padding:2px 6px 2px;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:6px;">
    <div>
      <div style="font-family:'Source Serif 4',Georgia,serif;font-weight:700;font-size:20px;color:#23304a;">
        Marriage age by year,
        <span id="db-gender" style="color:#2f4b7c;">Grooms</span>, 2003&ndash;2024
      </div>
      <div style="font-family:Inter,sans-serif;font-size:14px;font-weight:500;color:#3a4356;margin-top:2px;">
        <b>Dumbbell:</b> median first marriage &rarr; re-marriage age &nbsp;&bull;&nbsp; <b>Bars:</b> age distribution (mean + mode), across all marriages
      </div>
    </div>
    <div class="dumbbell-toggle" role="group" aria-label="Choose gender, hover to switch">
      <button id="db-btn-groom" class="active-groom">Grooms</button>
      <button id="db-btn-bride">Brides</button>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:8px;padding:2px 8px 2px;">
    <div id="db-legend" style="display:flex;gap:22px;font-size:13px;color:#5f6b7a;flex-wrap:wrap;"></div>
    <div style="display:flex;gap:16px;">
      <label class="db-checkbox">
        <input type="checkbox" class="chk-mean" id="db-chk-mean"> Show mean
      </label>
      <label class="db-checkbox">
        <input type="checkbox" class="chk-mode" id="db-chk-mode"> Show mode
      </label>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div id="db-chart" style="width:100%;height:500px;overflow-y:auto;overflow-x:hidden;border-top:1px solid #efe9dd;"></div>
  <div class="small" style="padding:4px 8px 4px;font-size:11.5px;color:#8a8577;line-height:1.55;">
    <span style="color:#2f4b7c;font-weight:700;">Source:</span> Singapore DOS, Tables M830169 (median ages), M830170 (age-band counts).
    &nbsp;<span style="font-weight:900;color:#5f6b7a;">&middot;</span>&nbsp;
    <span style="color:#2f4b7c;font-weight:700;">Marriages during Covid:</span> 2020&ndash;2021 is highlighted in <span style="color:#b5651d;font-weight:700;">Orange</span>.
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function(){
  var DATA = MARRIAGE_DATA;
  // AGE_BANDS/BAND_MID/GROOM_BANDS/BRIDE_BANDS/showTip/hideTip: shared header globals (_head-include.html)

  // barLo/barHi bound the histogram's colour scale: barLo is a near-white starting tint so empty bands stay quiet, barHi is a clearly saturated version of the gender colour.
  var PAL={
    groom:{first:'#7b9acc',remar:'#2f4b7c',bar:'#7d9bc9',barLo:'#eef2fa',barHi:'#5f84bd',line:'#152c4d',label:'Grooms',title:'#2f4b7c',bandKey:GROOM_BANDS,imgFirst:GROOM_IMG_FIRST,imgRemar:GROOM_IMG_REMAR},
    bride:{first:'#d98fae',remar:'#a8456b',bar:'#cf82a4',barLo:'#fbeef4',barHi:'#c06b93',line:'#5e2138',label:'Brides',title:'#a8456b',bandKey:BRIDE_BANDS,imgFirst:BRIDE_IMG_FIRST,imgRemar:BRIDE_IMG_REMAR}
  };
  // WCAG 3:1 graphical-object contrast against both bar tints
  var MODE_COLOR='#5fe0c0', MEAN_COLOR='#ff5a36';

  // One shared coordinate system for both geoms (bars + dumbbell): x = age, y = year row.
  // This is what keeps the visual a single plot rather than two linked charts.
  var W=1000, mL=64, mR=52, mT=54, AMIN=16, AMAX=68;
  var rowH=70, n=DATA.length, H=mT+rowH*n+16;
  var barMaxH = rowH*0.58; // bars capped well short of full row height so they read as texture, not a competing chart
  var IMG_R=20;

  var xs = d3.scaleLinear().domain([AMIN,AMAX]).range([mL, W-mR]);
  function rowTop(i){ return mT + rowH*i; }
  var COVID = [2020,2021];
  var showMean = false, showMode = false;

  function esc(v){ return v.toFixed(1); }

  function weightedMean(counts){
    var num=0, den=0;
    counts.forEach(function(c,i){ num+=c*BAND_MID[i]; den+=c; });
    return num/den;
  }
  function modeIndex(counts){
    var best=0;
    counts.forEach(function(c,i){ if(c>counts[best]) best=i; });
    return best;
  }

  // svg selected once and reused across redraws (children cleared each time) instead of replaced on every hover
  function chartSvg(){
    var svg = d3.select('#db-chart').selectAll('svg').data([null]);
    svg = svg.enter().append('svg').merge(svg)
      .attr('viewBox', '0 0 '+W+' '+H).attr('width','100%')
      .attr('role','img').attr('aria-label','Dumbbell chart of median marriage age, with each year\'s age-band distribution layered behind it')
      .style('font-family','Inter,sans-serif');
    svg.selectAll('*').remove();
    return svg;
  }

  function haloText(sel){
    return sel.attr('paint-order','stroke').attr('stroke','#ffffff').attr('stroke-width',3).attr('stroke-linejoin','round');
  }

  function draw(g){
    var p = PAL[g];
    var svg = chartSvg();

    var ticks = d3.range(20, 66, 5);
    var tickG = svg.selectAll(null).data(ticks).enter().append('g');
    tickG.append('line')
      .attr('x1', function(a){ return xs(a); }).attr('y1', mT-8)
      .attr('x2', function(a){ return xs(a); }).attr('y2', H-6).attr('stroke', '#eee6d8');
    tickG.append('text')
      .attr('x', function(a){ return xs(a); }).attr('y', mT-14)
      .attr('text-anchor', 'middle').attr('font-size', 11).attr('fill', '#9aa2ad').text(function(a){ return a; });
    svg.append('text').attr('x', mL+(W-mL-mR)/2).attr('y', 16).attr('text-anchor', 'middle')
      .attr('font-size', 12).attr('fill', '#5f6b7a').text('Age (years)');

    var rows = svg.selectAll(null).data(DATA).enter().append('g')
      .attr('transform', function(d,i){ return 'translate(0,'+rowTop(i)+')'; });

    rows.each(function(d){
      var row = d3.select(this);
      var counts = p.bandKey[d.y];
      var v1 = (g==='groom' ? d.gf : d.bf), v2 = (g==='groom' ? d.gr : d.br), gap = v2-v1;
      var isCovid = COVID.indexOf(d.y) > -1;
      var baseY = rowH*0.86;

      // hit area drives the hover tooltip; kept behind everything else in this row
      row.append('rect').attr('x', 0).attr('y', 0).attr('width', W).attr('height', rowH)
        .attr('fill', 'transparent')
        .on('mousemove', function(event){
          // "all marriages" is folded into the header line itself, right next to the numbers
          // it qualifies, instead of a separate disclaimer sentence nobody reads twice
          if(!counts){ showTip(event, '<b>'+d.y+'</b><br>Age-band counts not yet published by SingStat &mdash; dumbbell only'); return; }
          var mean = weightedMean(counts), modeI = modeIndex(counts);
          showTip(event, '<b>'+d.y+', all marriages</b><br>Mean age '+mean.toFixed(1)+' &middot; Mode band '+AGE_BANDS[modeI]);
        })
        .on('mouseleave', hideTip);

      // background ridge: this year's age-band histogram, capped short so the dumbbell
      // above stays the focal geom even though both share the same axes. Each bar's fill
      // is scaled to its own count, light for sparse bands, saturating toward a clearly
      // darker gender colour for the peak. A power scale (exponent < 1) lifts the mid-sized
      // bands too, so the whole shape reads at a glance instead of only the tallest bar.
      var barW = (xs(BAND_MID[1]) - xs(BAND_MID[0])) * 0.72;
      if(counts){
        var maxCount = d3.max(counts);
        var barColor = d3.scalePow().exponent(0.55).domain([0, maxCount]).range([p.barLo, p.barHi]);
        row.selectAll(null).data(counts).enter().append('rect')
          .attr('x', function(c,i){ return xs(BAND_MID[i]) - barW/2; })
          .attr('y', function(c){ return baseY - (c/maxCount)*barMaxH; })
          .attr('width', barW)
          .attr('height', function(c){ return (c/maxCount)*barMaxH; })
          .attr('fill', function(c){ return barColor(c); });
      }

      // mean/mode marks drawn right after the bars, so they sit BEHIND the connector line,
      // endpoint badge icons, and labels rather than covering them
      if(counts){
        var mean = weightedMean(counts), modeI = modeIndex(counts);
        row.append('line').attr('class','mean-mark')
          .attr('x1', xs(mean)).attr('y1', baseY-barMaxH-4).attr('x2', xs(mean)).attr('y2', baseY+2)
          .attr('stroke', MEAN_COLOR).attr('stroke-width', 2.8).attr('stroke-dasharray','5,3')
          .style('display', showMean ? null : 'none');
        row.append('rect').attr('class','mode-mark')
          .attr('x', xs(BAND_MID[modeI])-barW/2).attr('y', baseY-(counts[modeI]/maxCount)*barMaxH)
          .attr('width', barW).attr('height', (counts[modeI]/maxCount)*barMaxH)
          .attr('fill', 'none').attr('stroke', MODE_COLOR).attr('stroke-width', 2.2)
          .style('display', showMode ? null : 'none');
      }

      // line sits well clear of the bar peaks (only the tallest bars graze it), so labels
      // don't have to compete with bar fill; the white halo covers what little overlap remains
      var lineY = baseY - barMaxH*0.95;
      var x1 = xs(v1), x2 = xs(v2);

      // stroked in the gender's dark remar tone (not the light bar tint), so the connector
      // reads clearly against the histogram instead of blending into it
      row.append('line').attr('x1', x1).attr('y1', lineY).attr('x2', x2).attr('y2', lineY)
        .attr('stroke', p.line).attr('stroke-width', 2.2).attr('stroke-linecap', 'round');

      haloText(row.append('text').attr('x', (x1+x2)/2).attr('y', lineY-9).attr('text-anchor', 'middle')
        .attr('font-size', 12).attr('fill', '#3a4356').attr('font-weight', 700)).text(gap.toFixed(1));

      row.append('image').attr('href', p.imgFirst).attr('x', x1-IMG_R).attr('y', lineY-IMG_R).attr('width', 2*IMG_R).attr('height', 2*IMG_R);
      row.append('image').attr('href', p.imgRemar).attr('x', x2-IMG_R).attr('y', lineY-IMG_R).attr('width', 2*IMG_R).attr('height', 2*IMG_R);

      // endpoint values sit beside their marker rather than stacked below it, so they can't
      // collide with each other even on years where the dumbbell itself is short
      haloText(row.append('text').attr('x', x1-IMG_R-5).attr('y', lineY+5).attr('text-anchor', 'end')
        .attr('font-size', 13.5).attr('fill', p.first).attr('font-weight', 600)).text(esc(v1));
      haloText(row.append('text').attr('x', x2+IMG_R+5).attr('y', lineY+5).attr('text-anchor', 'start')
        .attr('font-size', 13.5).attr('fill', p.remar).attr('font-weight', 700)).text(esc(v2));

      haloText(row.append('text').attr('x', mL-14).attr('y', lineY+4).attr('text-anchor', 'end')
        .attr('font-size', 12.5).attr('fill', isCovid ? '#b5651d' : '#5f6b7a')
        .attr('font-weight', isCovid ? 700 : 500)).text(d.y);
    });

    d3.select('#db-legend').html(
      '<span><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:'+p.first+';margin-right:6px;"></span>First marriage</span>'+
      '<span><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:'+p.remar+';margin-right:6px;"></span>Re-marriage</span>'+
      '<span><span style="display:inline-block;width:16px;height:2px;background:'+p.line+';margin-right:6px;vertical-align:middle;"></span>Connector = gap in years</span>'+
      '<span><span style="display:inline-block;width:12px;height:8px;background:'+p.barHi+';margin-right:6px;"></span>Age-band distribution (all marriages)</span>'
    );
    var gEl = document.getElementById('db-gender');
    gEl.textContent = p.label; gEl.style.color = p.title;
    document.getElementById('db-btn-groom').className = (g==='groom' ? 'active-groom' : '');
    document.getElementById('db-btn-bride').className = (g==='bride' ? 'active-bride' : '');
  }

  document.getElementById('db-btn-groom').addEventListener('mouseenter', function(){ draw('groom'); });
  document.getElementById('db-btn-bride').addEventListener('mouseenter', function(){ draw('bride'); });
  document.getElementById('db-btn-groom').addEventListener('click', function(){ draw('groom'); });
  document.getElementById('db-btn-bride').addEventListener('click', function(){ draw('bride'); });
  document.getElementById('db-chk-mean').addEventListener('change', function(e){
    showMean = e.target.checked;
    d3.selectAll('.mean-mark').style('display', showMean ? null : 'none');
  });
  document.getElementById('db-chk-mode').addEventListener('change', function(e){
    showMode = e.target.checked;
    d3.selectAll('.mode-mark').style('display', showMode ? null : 'none');
  });

  draw('groom');
})();
</script>
```

# Data Engineering {.section-divider}

::: section-sub
From SingStat raw exports to a clean dataset
:::

## Data sources {.smaller}

::::::::: columns

::: {.box .slate-box .small-box}

| year | groom_first | groom_remarry | bride_first | bride_remarry |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| 2003 | `r marriage$groom_first[marriage$year==2003]` | `r marriage$groom_remarry[marriage$year==2003]` | `r marriage$bride_first[marriage$year==2003]` | `r marriage$bride_remarry[marriage$year==2003]` |
| 2010 | `r marriage$groom_first[marriage$year==2010]` | `r marriage$groom_remarry[marriage$year==2010]` | `r marriage$bride_first[marriage$year==2010]` | `r marriage$bride_remarry[marriage$year==2010]` |
| 2024 | `r marriage$groom_first[marriage$year==2024]` | `r marriage$groom_remarry[marriage$year==2024]` | `r marriage$bride_first[marriage$year==2024]` | `r marriage$bride_remarry[marriage$year==2024]` |

: Dumbbell input (pulled live from `marriage`, computed in the setup chunk from `data/clean/M830169_cleaned.csv`). Gap columns (`groom_gap`/`bride_gap`) are computed from these afterward.
:::
:::::

::::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.box .slate-box .small-box}
**M830170** : Marriages by Age Group and Previous Marital Status [@singstat_m830170]
:::

::: compact-table
| year | groom_25to29 | bride_25to29 | groom_30to34 | bride_30to34 |
|----|----|----|----|----|
| 2003 | `r bands[["25-29"]][bands$year==2003 & bands$gender=="Grooms"]` | `r bands[["25-29"]][bands$year==2003 & bands$gender=="Brides"]` | `r bands[["30-34"]][bands$year==2003 & bands$gender=="Grooms"]` | `r bands[["30-34"]][bands$year==2003 & bands$gender=="Brides"]` |
| 2010 | `r bands[["25-29"]][bands$year==2010 & bands$gender=="Grooms"]` | `r bands[["25-29"]][bands$year==2010 & bands$gender=="Brides"]` | `r bands[["30-34"]][bands$year==2010 & bands$gender=="Grooms"]` | `r bands[["30-34"]][bands$year==2010 & bands$gender=="Brides"]` |
| 2015 | `r bands[["25-29"]][bands$year==2015 & bands$gender=="Grooms"]` | `r bands[["25-29"]][bands$year==2015 & bands$gender=="Brides"]` | `r bands[["30-34"]][bands$year==2015 & bands$gender=="Grooms"]` | `r bands[["30-34"]][bands$year==2015 & bands$gender=="Brides"]` |

: Background histogram input (pulled live from `bands`, computed in the setup chunk from `data/clean/M830170_cleaned.csv`), 2 of 10 age bands shown. Full table is year × gender × band, 2003–2023.
:::
:::::
:::::::::

- **Two tables, one role each.** M830169 drives the dumbbell (median ages, by gender); M830170 drives the background histogram (age-band counts, not split by marriage order).
- **Same source, no external joins.** Both from SingStat TableBuilder, combined by year and gender, not merged row-for-row.
- **Reproducible.** Stable table IDs, dated exports: 2003–2024 for M830169, 2003–2023 for M830170 (SingStat's age-band table doesn't cover 2024 yet).

## From raw export to clean table {.smaller}

The SingStat file is not a clean rectangle.
Ten metadata rows precede the table, marriage type and sex are implied by row text and indentation, and year headers carry trailing whitespace.
Five sequential stages resolve this.

::: small

:::

::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fit-col .compact-table}
| Stage (M830169) | Action |
|----|----|
| **1. Import** | Skip 10 metadata rows, keep year headers as a vector |
| **2. Baseline check** | Record raw shape, missing cells, year range |
| **3. Label** | Tag type/gender from the `" - "` delimiter |
| **4. Reshape, filter** | Pivot long, filter Total Marriages, year ≥ 2003 |
| **5. Gap, schema** | Pivot wide, compute gaps, validate |
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fit-col .compact-table}
| Stage (M830170)        | Action                              |
|------------------------|-------------------------------------|
| **1. Import**          | Skip metadata rows, read raw CSV    |
| **2. Label**           | Tag gender from header text         |
| **3. Reshape, filter** | Pivot long, keep Total Marriages    |
| **4. Pivot by band**   | Pivot wide, keyed on age band       |
| **5. Schema**          | Validate lookup, write cleaned file |
:::
::::
:::::::

::: small
Each stage reads the output of the one before and produces a new object, so any single step stays inspectable and re-runnable on its own.
:::

## The pipeline in code: Import and baseline {.smaller}

The same five stages as the previous slide, now with the full, unfolded code, starting with the two setup stages for M830169.

**Stage 1 : Import**

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
library(tidyverse)

raw <- read_csv("data/raw/M830169_raw.csv", skip = 10, col_names = FALSE)
years_header <- raw |> slice(1) |> select(-1) |> unlist() |> as.numeric()
```

::: small
Skips the ten metadata rows and reads the table raw, then pulls row 1's year labels (1961…2025) into their own vector, since Stage 3 reattaches them as real column names.
:::

**Stage 2 : Baseline check**

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
baseline <- list(
  n_rows    = nrow(raw),
  n_missing = sum(is.na(raw))
)
```

::: small
Records the row count and missing-cell count straight off the untouched import, so Stage 5's checks have a good reference to compare against.
:::

## The pipeline in code: Label, reshape and filter {.smaller}

The two heaviest stages: turning row text into type/gender columns, then pivoting long and back to wide.

**Stage 3 : Label**

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
marriage <- raw |>
  set_names(c("X1", as.character(years_header))) |>
  slice(-1) |>
  mutate(label = str_trim(X1),
         is_header = str_detect(label, " - "),
         type   = if_else(is_header, str_split_i(label, " - ", 1), NA),
         gender = if_else(is_header, str_split_i(label, " - ", 2), NA)) |>
  fill(type, gender, .direction = "down") |>
  mutate(order = if_else(is_header, "All", label))
```

::: small
The Stage 1 year vector is reattached as real column names *first*, while the frame is still just X1 + 65 year columns; only then does `mutate()` derive `label`/`type`/`gender`/`order`.
Renaming after those columns exist would silently misalign names to columns once `mutate()` has appended them.
Header rows like `"Total Marriages - Grooms"` give up type and gender via the `" - "` delimiter, and `fill()` carries those values down onto the indented data rows beneath them.
:::

**Stage 4 : Reshape and filter**

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
marriage <- marriage |>
  pivot_longer(-c(X1,label,is_header,type,gender,order),
               names_to = "year", values_to = "age") |>
  filter(type == "Total Marriages",
         order %in% c("First Marriages","Remarriages"),
         as.integer(year) >= 2003, as.integer(year) <= 2024) |>
  select(year, gender, order, age) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(gender, order), values_from = age) |>
  rename(groom_first   = `Grooms_First Marriages`,
         groom_remarry = `Grooms_Remarriages`,
         bride_first   = `Brides_First Marriages`,
         bride_remarry = `Brides_Remarriages`)
```

::: small
Pivots to one row per year, keeps only combined-order Total Marriages for first marriages and remarriages from 2003 to 2024, then selects down to just `year`/`gender`/`order`/`age` before pivoting wide.
That select matters: `pivot_wider()` treats every column not named in `names_from`/`values_from` as part of the row identity, and `X1`/`label`/`is_header` still differ between the "First Marriages" row and the "Remarriages" row for the same year -- skip the select and you get 44 rows instead of 22.
Renames the four resulting columns to `groom_first`, `groom_remarry`, `bride_first`, `bride_remarry`.
:::

## The pipeline in code: Schema, gap and M830170 {#pipeline-code-3 .smaller}

The final validation stage for M830169, and the condensed pattern that produces M830170.

**Stage 5 : Gap and schema**

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
marriage <- marriage |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  mutate(groom_gap = round(groom_remarry - groom_first, 1),
         bride_gap = round(bride_remarry - bride_first, 1))

stopifnot(nrow(marriage) == 22,
          all(marriage$groom_gap > 0, marriage$bride_gap > 0),
          n_distinct(marriage$year) == nrow(marriage))

write_csv(marriage, "data/clean/M830169_cleaned.csv")
```

::: small
Computes the gap columns once so every downstream chart reads the same number, checks the row count and gap sign against the expected shape, and writes the validated table every other slide reads from.
:::

**M830170 : Condensed**

No baseline-check or gap stage is needed here, so the same skip/label/reshape pattern collapses into one chain.

```{r}
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
raw170 <- read_csv("data/raw/M830170_raw.csv", skip = 10, col_names = FALSE)
years170 <- raw170 |> slice(1) |> select(-1) |> unlist() |> as.numeric()

bands <- raw170 |>
  set_names(c("X1", as.character(years170))) |>
  slice(-1) |>
  mutate(label = str_trim(X1),
         gender = if_else(str_detect(label, " - "), str_split_i(label, " - ", 2), NA),
         age_band = if_else(str_detect(label, " - "), NA, label)) |>
  fill(gender, .direction = "down") |>
  filter(!is.na(age_band)) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(X1, label, gender, age_band), names_to = "year", values_to = "count") |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year)) |>
  select(year, gender, age_band, count) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = age_band, values_from = count) |>
  select(year, gender, `Under 20`, `20-24`, `25-29`, `30-34`, `35-39`,
         `40-44`, `45-49`, `50-54`, `55-59`, `60 & Over`) |>
  arrange(year, gender)

stopifnot(nrow(bands) == 42)
write_csv(bands, "data/clean/M830170_cleaned.csv")
```

::: small
Same fix as M830169's Stage 3: year columns are renamed before any label/gender columns are derived.
The original condensed version of this code never reattached year labels at all, so its "year" column would have held literal column names instead of real years, another bug that only surfaced once this was actually run.
Also selects down to `year`/`gender`/`age_band`/`count` before pivoting wide, for the same reason as M830169's Stage 4: `pivot_wider()` treats every leftover column as part of the row identity, and `X1`/`label` still vary per age band, so skipping this select would stop rows from collapsing to one per year/gender.
Keeps only the non-header age-band rows under each gender's "Total Marriages" section and pivots wide once on age band.
The check is 42 rows (21 published years × 2 genders), not 44 — SingStat's age-band table doesn't cover 2024 yet as of this pull, matching the dumbbell chart's own "not yet published" tooltip for that year.
:::

# Data Analysis {.section-divider}

::: section-sub
Three statistical analyses of the marriage-age data
:::

## A1: Brides' First-Marriage Age Rises Twice as Fast {.smaller}

::: box
Brides' median age at first marriage is increasing at roughly twice the rate observed for grooms.
:::

:::::: {.columns .top-align}
:::: {.column width="46%"}
::: frame
- Brides' first-marriage age increases by **`r round(coef(fit_b)["year"], 2)` years per year** (95% CI `r round(ci_b[1], 2)` to `r round(ci_b[2], 2)`, R² `r round(r2_b, 2)`).
- Grooms' first-marriage age increases by **`r round(coef(fit_g)["year"], 2)` years per year**, less than half the rate for brides (95% CI `r round(ci_g[1], 2)` to `r round(ci_g[2], 2)`, R² `r round(r2_g, 2)`).
- Between 2003 and 2024, this corresponds to a change of approximately **`r round(marriage$bride_first[marriage$year==2024] - marriage$bride_first[marriage$year==2003], 1)` years** for brides, compared with **`r round(marriage$groom_first[marriage$year==2024] - marriage$groom_first[marriage$year==2003], 1)` years** for grooms.
- The difference between the two slopes is statistically significant (*t*(`r round(df_diff,0)`) = `r round(t_diff, 2)`, *p* \< .001).
:::
::::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{=html}
<div class="mini-chart-wrap"><div id="a1-chart-wrap" style="width:100%;"></div></div>
<script>
(function(){
  var DATA = MARRIAGE_DATA; // only .y/.gf/.bf used here
  var W = 480, H = 180, margin = {left:34, right:14, top:26, bottom:26};

  var x = d3.scaleLinear()
    .domain(d3.extent(DATA, function(d){ return d.y; }))
    .range([margin.left, W - margin.right]);

  var vals = DATA.flatMap(function(d){ return [d.gf, d.bf]; });
  var y = d3.scaleLinear()
    .domain([d3.min(vals) - 1, d3.max(vals) + 1])
    .range([H - margin.bottom, margin.top]);

  var svg = d3.select('#a1-chart-wrap').append('svg')
    .attr('viewBox', '0 0 ' + W + ' ' + H)
    .attr('width', '100%')
    .attr('role', 'img')
    .attr('aria-label', 'Median first-marriage age by year, grooms and brides. Interactive: hover a point for its exact value.');

  svg.append('text').attr('x', 10).attr('y', 16).attr('class', 'chart-title')
    .text('Median first-marriage age, 2003 to 2024');

  // y-axis gridlines + tick labels so the chart has a readable scale even
  // without hovering (matters for print/PDF export, not just on-screen use)
  var yTicksA1 = y.ticks(4);
  svg.selectAll(null).data(yTicksA1).enter().append('line')
    .attr('x1', margin.left).attr('x2', W - margin.right)
    .attr('y1', function(v){ return y(v); }).attr('y2', function(v){ return y(v); })
    .attr('stroke', '#eee6d8');
  svg.selectAll(null).data(yTicksA1).enter().append('text')
    .attr('x', margin.left - 6).attr('y', function(v){ return y(v) + 3; })
    .attr('text-anchor', 'end').attr('font-size', 10).attr('fill', '#9aa2ad')
    .text(function(v){ return v; });

  ['gf', 'bf'].forEach(function(key){
    var color = key === 'gf' ? '#2f4b7c' : '#b5651d';
    var line = d3.line().x(function(d){ return x(d.y); }).y(function(d){ return y(d[key]); });
    svg.append('path').datum(DATA).attr('d', line).attr('fill', 'none').attr('stroke', color).attr('stroke-width', 2.4);

    // large invisible hit circle over each small visible dot keeps hover targets comfortable at this dot size
    var points = svg.selectAll(null).data(DATA).enter().append('g');
    points.append('circle')
      .attr('cx', function(d){ return x(d.y); }).attr('cy', function(d){ return y(d[key]); })
      .attr('r', 7).attr('fill', color).attr('opacity', 0)
      .on('mousemove', function(event, d){ showTip(event, '<b>' + d.y + '</b><br>Grooms: ' + d.gf + '<br>Brides: ' + d.bf); })
      .on('mouseleave', hideTip);
    points.append('circle')
      .attr('cx', function(d){ return x(d.y); }).attr('cy', function(d){ return y(d[key]); })
      .attr('r', 2.6).attr('fill', color);
  });

  var last = DATA[DATA.length - 1];
  svg.append('text').attr('x', W - 14).attr('y', y(last.gf) - 8).attr('class', 'series-label groom').text('Grooms');
  svg.append('text').attr('x', W - 14).attr('y', y(last.bf) + 16).attr('class', 'series-label bride').text('Brides');
  svg.append('text').attr('x', margin.left).attr('y', H - 6).attr('class', 'axis-label').text(DATA[0].y);
  svg.append('text').attr('x', W - margin.right).attr('y', H - 6).attr('class', 'axis-label axis-label-end').text(last.y);
})();
</script>
```

The original chart's four overlapping lines display as a single shared slope.
The two separate rates are only visible when each gender is fitted independently.
:::
::::::

Method: `lm(median_age ~ year)` per gender, 22 annual observations each.
Significance of both slopes and of their difference confirmed by two-sided *t*-tests, with 95% CIs from the OLS standard errors.

## A2: First Marriage and Re-marriage Are Drifting Further Apart {.smaller}

::: box
The gap between first-marriage age and re-marriage age widened for both genders between 2003 and 2024.
:::

:::::: {.columns .top-align}
:::: {.column width="46%"}
::: frame
- Groom gap increased from **`r marriage$groom_gap[marriage$year==2003]` to `r marriage$groom_gap[marriage$year==2024]` years**, at a rate of `r round(coef(fit_gg)["year"],2)` years per year (95% CI `r round(ci_gg[1],2)` to `r round(ci_gg[2],2)`, R² `r round(r2_gg,2)`).
- Bride gap increased from **`r marriage$bride_gap[marriage$year==2003]` to `r marriage$bride_gap[marriage$year==2024]` years**, at a rate of `r round(coef(fit_bg)["year"],2)` years per year (95% CI `r round(ci_bg[1],2)` to `r round(ci_bg[2],2)`, R² `r round(r2_bg,2)`).
- Both trends are statistically significant (*p* \< .001 for each).
- Both gaps dip in 2020 to 2021 (highlighted on the chart), consistent with pandemic-era disruption to remarriages, for example couples delaying weddings or divorces being deferred by court closures and then processed once restrictions eased.
:::
::::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{=html}
<div class="mini-chart-wrap"><div id="a2-chart-wrap" style="width:100%;"></div></div>
<script>
(function(){
  // gap columns derived from shared source instead of re-typed, so they can't drift from the dumbbell chart
  var DATA = MARRIAGE_DATA.map(function(d){
    return {y:d.y, gg:+(d.gr-d.gf).toFixed(1), bg:+(d.br-d.bf).toFixed(1)};
  });
  var W = 480, H = 180, margin = {left:34, right:14, top:26, bottom:26};

  var x = d3.scaleLinear()
    .domain(d3.extent(DATA, function(d){ return d.y; }))
    .range([margin.left, W - margin.right]);

  var vals = DATA.flatMap(function(d){ return [d.gg, d.bg]; });
  var y = d3.scaleLinear()
    .domain([d3.min(vals) - 1, d3.max(vals) + 1])
    .range([H - margin.bottom, margin.top]);

  var svg = d3.select('#a2-chart-wrap').append('svg')
    .attr('viewBox', '0 0 ' + W + ' ' + H)
    .attr('width', '100%')
    .attr('role', 'img')
    .attr('aria-label', 'Groom and bride gap between first marriage and re-marriage age, by year. Interactive: hover a point for its exact value. 2020 to 2021 is shaded and labelled as a COVID-19 related dip.');

  svg.append('text').attr('x', 10).attr('y', 16).attr('class', 'chart-title')
    .text('Gap: re-marriage age minus first-marriage age');

  // COVID-19 annotation: shade the 2020-2021 dip and label it directly on the
  // chart, rather than leaving the reader to notice the dip unexplained.
  var covidX0 = x(2020), covidX1 = x(2021);
  svg.append('rect')
    .attr('x', covidX0).attr('y', margin.top)
    .attr('width', covidX1 - covidX0).attr('height', H - margin.top - margin.bottom)
    .attr('fill', '#b5651d').attr('opacity', 0.08);
  // Anchor the label to the left of the band (not centered on it) so it
  // clears the "Groom gap" series label sitting at the chart's right edge,
  // and point the leader line at the true lowest vertex (2021), not the
  // midpoint of the shaded span.
  var covidLabelX = covidX0 - 6, covidLabelY = margin.top + 9;
  svg.append('text')
    .attr('x', covidLabelX).attr('y', covidLabelY)
    .attr('text-anchor', 'end').attr('font-size', 9.5).attr('fill', '#b5651d').attr('font-weight', 600)
    .text('COVID-19');

  // y-axis gridlines + tick labels, same fix as the A1 chart above
  var yTicksA2 = y.ticks(4);
  svg.selectAll(null).data(yTicksA2).enter().append('line')
    .attr('x1', margin.left).attr('x2', W - margin.right)
    .attr('y1', function(v){ return y(v); }).attr('y2', function(v){ return y(v); })
    .attr('stroke', '#eee6d8');
  svg.selectAll(null).data(yTicksA2).enter().append('text')
    .attr('x', margin.left - 6).attr('y', function(v){ return y(v) + 3; })
    .attr('text-anchor', 'end').attr('font-size', 10).attr('fill', '#9aa2ad')
    .text(function(v){ return v; });

  ['gg', 'bg'].forEach(function(key){
    var color = key === 'gg' ? '#2f4b7c' : '#b5651d';
    var line = d3.line().x(function(d){ return x(d.y); }).y(function(d){ return y(d[key]); });
    svg.append('path').datum(DATA).attr('d', line).attr('fill', 'none').attr('stroke', color).attr('stroke-width', 2.4);

    var points = svg.selectAll(null).data(DATA).enter().append('g');
    points.append('circle')
      .attr('cx', function(d){ return x(d.y); }).attr('cy', function(d){ return y(d[key]); })
      .attr('r', 7).attr('fill', color).attr('opacity', 0)
      .on('mousemove', function(event, d){ showTip(event, '<b>' + d.y + '</b><br>Groom gap: ' + d.gg + 'y<br>Bride gap: ' + d.bg + 'y'); })
      .on('mouseleave', hideTip);
    points.append('circle')
      .attr('cx', function(d){ return x(d.y); }).attr('cy', function(d){ return y(d[key]); })
      .attr('r', 2.6).attr('fill', color);
  });

  var last = DATA[DATA.length - 1];
  svg.append('text').attr('x', W - 14).attr('y', y(last.gg) - 8).attr('class', 'series-label groom').text('Groom gap');
  svg.append('text').attr('x', W - 14).attr('y', y(last.bg) + 16).attr('class', 'series-label bride').text('Bride gap');
  svg.append('text').attr('x', margin.left).attr('y', H - 6).attr('class', 'axis-label').text(DATA[0].y);
  svg.append('text').attr('x', W - margin.right).attr('y', H - 6).attr('class', 'axis-label axis-label-end').text(last.y);
})();
</script>
```

The lower R² here compared with A1 is expected, since re-marriages are far fewer and their annual medians are more sensitive to short-term fluctuations.
Both trends remain statistically significant (*p* \< .001).
:::
::::::

Method: `lm(gap ~ year)` per gender, 22 annual observations each, with 95% CIs from the OLS standard errors.

## A3: Grooms and Brides Are Closing Their Age Gap {.smaller}

::: {.box .slate-box}
The difference between groom and bride first-marriage age narrowed between 2003 and 2024, while both ages continued to increase.
:::

:::::: {.columns .top-align}
:::: {.column width="46%"}
::: frame
- Gender gap narrowed from **`r round(gender_gap[marriage$year==2003],1)` to `r round(gender_gap[marriage$year==2024],1)` years** (mean `r round(mean(gender_gap),1)`).
- Groom and bride first-marriage ages are highly correlated (r = `r round(ct$estimate,2)`, 95% CI `r round(ct$conf.int[1],2)` to `r round(ct$conf.int[2],2)`, *p* \< .001, *n* = 22).
- This indicates a consistent convergence rather than a random fluctuation. Bride age is increasing at a faster rate, which reduces the gap.
:::
::::

::: {.column width="54%"}
```{=html}
<div class="mini-chart-wrap"><div id="a3-chart-wrap" style="width:100%;"></div></div>
<script>
(function(){
  var DATA = MARRIAGE_DATA; // only .y/.gf/.bf used here
  var W = 480, H = 180, margin = {left:34, right:16, top:26, bottom:30};

  var gVals = DATA.map(function(d){ return d.gf; }), bVals = DATA.map(function(d){ return d.bf; });
  var x = d3.scaleLinear().domain([d3.min(gVals) - 0.3, d3.max(gVals) + 0.3]).range([margin.left, W - margin.right]);
  var y = d3.scaleLinear().domain([d3.min(bVals) - 0.3, d3.max(bVals) + 0.3]).range([H - margin.bottom, margin.top]);

  // least-squares fit of bride age on groom age, visual aid for r = 0.95 correlation
  var n = DATA.length, sx=0, sy=0, sxy=0, sxx=0;
  DATA.forEach(function(d){ sx+=d.gf; sy+=d.bf; sxy+=d.gf*d.bf; sxx+=d.gf*d.gf; });
  var slope = (n*sxy - sx*sy) / (n*sxx - sx*sx), intercept = (sy - slope*sx) / n;
  var [gMin, gMax] = x.domain();

  var svg = d3.select('#a3-chart-wrap').append('svg')
    .attr('viewBox', '0 0 ' + W + ' ' + H)
    .attr('width', '100%')
    .attr('role', 'img')
    .attr('aria-label', 'Groom median age plotted against bride median age, by year. Interactive: hover a point for its year.');

  svg.append('text').attr('x', 10).attr('y', 16).attr('class', 'chart-title')
    .text('Groom vs bride first-marriage age');

  svg.append('line').attr('x1', margin.left).attr('y1', H - margin.bottom).attr('x2', W - margin.right).attr('y2', H - margin.bottom).attr('stroke', '#e4ddd2');
  svg.append('line').attr('x1', margin.left).attr('y1', margin.top).attr('x2', margin.left).attr('y2', H - margin.bottom).attr('stroke', '#e4ddd2');

  // The fitted line predicts a y-value from x; at the x-domain's edges that
  // predicted y can fall outside the plotted y-range, which would otherwise
  // draw the line past the chart's own border. Clamp each endpoint to the
  // visible y-domain (and solve back for the matching x) before drawing.
  var yDom = y.domain();
  function clampToPlot(gx){
    var gy = slope * gx + intercept;
    if (gy < yDom[0]) { gx = (yDom[0] - intercept) / slope; gy = yDom[0]; }
    else if (gy > yDom[1]) { gx = (yDom[1] - intercept) / slope; gy = yDom[1]; }
    return [gx, gy];
  }
  var p1 = clampToPlot(gMin), p2 = clampToPlot(gMax);
  svg.append('line')
    .attr('x1', x(p1[0])).attr('y1', y(p1[1]))
    .attr('x2', x(p2[0])).attr('y2', y(p2[1]))
    .attr('stroke', '#c8791f').attr('stroke-width', 1.6).attr('stroke-dasharray', '4,3');

  // numeric tick labels on both axes -- the lines were already there, but
  // with no numbers a reader had no way to read an approximate value
  var xTicksA3 = x.ticks(4), yTicksA3 = y.ticks(4);
  svg.selectAll(null).data(xTicksA3).enter().append('text')
    .attr('x', function(v){ return x(v); }).attr('y', H - margin.bottom + 12)
    .attr('text-anchor', 'middle').attr('font-size', 10).attr('fill', '#9aa2ad')
    .text(function(v){ return v.toFixed(0); });
  svg.selectAll(null).data(yTicksA3).enter().append('text')
    .attr('x', margin.left - 6).attr('y', function(v){ return y(v) + 3; })
    .attr('text-anchor', 'end').attr('font-size', 10).attr('fill', '#9aa2ad')
    .text(function(v){ return v.toFixed(0); });

  var points = svg.selectAll(null).data(DATA).enter().append('g');
  points.append('circle')
    .attr('cx', function(d){ return x(d.gf); }).attr('cy', function(d){ return y(d.bf); })
    .attr('r', 7).attr('fill', '#3d5a80').attr('opacity', 0)
    .on('mousemove', function(event, d){ showTip(event, '<b>' + d.y + '</b><br>Groom: ' + d.gf + '<br>Bride: ' + d.bf); })
    .on('mouseleave', hideTip);
  points.append('circle')
    .attr('cx', function(d){ return x(d.gf); }).attr('cy', function(d){ return y(d.bf); })
    .attr('r', 3.6).attr('fill', '#3d5a80');

  svg.append('text').attr('x', margin.left + (W-margin.left-margin.right)/2).attr('y', H - 6)
    .attr('text-anchor', 'middle').attr('class', 'axis-label').text('Groom median age, low to high →');
  svg.append('text').attr('x', 12).attr('y', margin.top + (H-margin.top-margin.bottom)/2)
    .attr('text-anchor', 'middle').attr('class', 'axis-label')
    .attr('transform', 'rotate(-90 12 ' + (margin.top + (H-margin.top-margin.bottom)/2) + ')')
    .text('Bride median age');
})();
</script>
```
:::
::::::

Method: Pearson correlation between groom and bride first-marriage age, 22 annual observations.
The dashed line is a least-squares fit shown as a visual aid, not a separate model.

# Takeaway {.section-divider}

::: section-sub
Findings, limitations and conclusion
:::

## Findings and Limitations {.smaller}

Three regressions back up what the chart shows.
Each comes with a caveat worth knowing.

::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="52%"}
::: box
**Findings**

- Bride first-marriage age rises about 0.14 years every year, versus 0.07 for grooms, almost double the rate (A1).
- The gap between first marriage and re-marriage widens for both genders: grooms from 11.1 to 13.9 years, brides from 7.6 to 10.0 years, over 2003 to 2024 (A2).
- The gender gap at first marriage narrows from 2.5 to 1.5 years, even though grooms' and brides' ages track each other closely (*r* = 0.95) (A3).
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="48%"}
::: {.box .slate-box}
**Caveats**

- Groom re-marriage age dips in 2020 to 2021, likely Covid-related court disruption, then recovers by 2022. This dip is why A2 fits more loosely than A1.
- The background histogram (M830170) counts all marriage orders together. SingStat does not publish it split by first marriage versus re-marriage, so it is a rough guide, not an exact match to the line it sits behind.
- Each regression uses 22 yearly medians (one per year, 2003 to 2024), not individual marriage records. The slopes describe the typical year, not any one couple.
- A3's correlation shows the two age series moving together. It does not show that one causes the other.
:::
::::
:::::::

::: small
Data: SingStat Table M830169 (median age by gender and marriage order) and Table M830170 (age band counts), 2003 to 2024.
Method: ordinary least squares regression fitted per gender for A1 and A2; Pearson correlation for A3.
Full model output on the A1 to A3 slides.
:::

## Future Improvements {.smaller}

The redesign fixes the six weaknesses named earlier.
These are the next steps we did not have scope or data for in this proposal.

::::::: columns
:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: box
**Using the data we already have**

- Split by marriage type. M830169 also records Civil and Muslim marriage ages, which this proposal collapses into Total. Showing them separately would tell us whether the closing gender gap holds across both types, or is driven by one.
- Fit the pandemic years separately. A short model for 2020 to 2021, apart from the rest of the series, would isolate that dip from the underlying trend and should tighten A2's fit.
- Extend the trend line forward. Projecting A1's fitted line past 2024, with a prediction interval, would give a concrete estimate for when the gender gap might close if the current pace holds.
:::
::::

:::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.box .slate-box}
**Needs data we do not have yet**

- A histogram split by marriage order. SingStat would need to publish age-band counts for first marriage and re-marriage separately, matching the exact line each histogram sits behind.
- Data before 2003. M830169 goes back to 1961. Adding those decades would show whether the closing gender gap is a recent shift or a longer-running one.
- A comparison country. A similarly structured dataset from a neighbouring country would show whether this pattern is specific to Singapore or part of a broader regional trend.
:::
::::
:::::::

::: small
None of these depend on this project's own pipeline.
They depend on SingStat, or another agency, publishing a table that does not currently exist in this form.
:::

## Conclusion {.smaller}

The original chart already showed that Singaporeans are marrying later.
It could not show two things the redesign brings out: how far first marriage now trails re-marriage, and which gender is closing that distance faster.

- Every one of the six weaknesses named at the start maps to a specific fix in the redesign, not a general restyle. A reader can check each one against the original chart directly.
- All three regressions are significant at *p* \< .001, based on 22 years of data (2003 to 2024).
- Brides are closing the age gap with grooms at first marriage, from 2.5 to 1.5 years, while both genders drift further from their own re-marriage age. The original chart's four overlapping lines make this pattern impossible to see; the redesign puts it in the connector labels directly.

```{=html}
<div class="weakness-grid" id="weakness-checklist"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const items = [
    ["W1", "Lines hard to tell apart"],
    ["W2", "Gender comparison buried"],
    ["W3", "Sparse points, no lookup"],
    ["W4", "Only median, no spread"],
    ["W5", "Gap never shown"],
    ["W6", "Colour-blind unsafe pairing"]
  ];
  document.getElementById("weakness-checklist").innerHTML = items.map(([code, label]) => `
    <div class="weakness-chip"><span class="accent">&#10003;</span><span><span class="slate">${code}</span> ${label}</span></div>
  `).join("");
})();
</script>
```

::: box
Singaporeans are not rejecting marriage.
They are delaying it, and who delays the most is changing.
:::
